title: Mobile app trends: 2026 edition
summary: A global benchmark of mobile app performance, combining industry context and 2026 marketing themes with performance analyses of gaming, e-commerce/shopping, and finance apps. The report uses aggregated, anonymized data from apps tracked by Adjust from January 2024 to January 2026, alongside some third-party industry estimates.

sections.title: Introduction: Evolution and opportunity in the mobile app industry
sections.summary: Introduces the growth outlook for mobile apps and the measurement and marketing challenges created by fragmented channels, evolving user behavior, and AI. It frames the report as a benchmark for gaming, e-commerce, and finance.
key_points: The report cites more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025, an estimated 5.8 billion unique smartphone users, and consumer spending of $167 billion, up 10.6% year over year.
It describes experimentation with AI, automation, and channel diversification as key features of 2025, while emphasizing the need for actionable data and cross-channel attribution.

In the chart “App install and session growth January 2024 - December 2025 (Global),” installs rose 10% and sessions 7% in 2025, compared with growth of 8% and 2%, respectively, in 2024; February 2025 installs were 13% below the yearly average, while December installs were 8% above it.
For Q1 2025 versus Q1 2026 global ATT opt-in rates, the industry average rose from 35% to 38%; gaming reached 39%, while e-commerce/shopping declined from 35% to 34%.

sections.title: AI transforms from strategic tool to core infrastructure in 2026
sections.summary: Describes AI being integrated into marketing and measurement workflows through data-analysis assistants, predictive audience segmentation, and practical generative-AI use. It notes that organizational maturity remains uneven.
key_points: AI assistants can query multi-channel data in natural language and surface analysis, reports, and visualizations in real time.
Audience segments are shifting from manually maintained static lists to dynamic groups based on behavior, intent, and likelihood to convert.

Generative AI is being used to test creative variants, model user journeys, and tailor in-app messaging; most organizations report low or moderate maturity, while a small advanced group reportedly achieved efficiency gains above 20%.

sections.title: Mobile-first approach evolves into multi-platform strategy
sections.summary: Argues that customer journeys now move across mobile web, desktop, apps, and other channels, making cross-platform measurement and deep linking important for attribution and conversion.
key_points: Only around 31% of marketers report complete satisfaction with their ability to unify and read data across platforms.
Cross-platform measurement connects activity such as a mobile-web session to an in-app conversion, revealing channel contributions beyond last-click credit.
The report recommends integrated measurement, high-quality deep linking, user segmentation, retargeting, and web-to-app solutions to reduce journey barriers.

sections.title: Key takeaways & methodology
sections.summary: Summarizes selected year-over-year findings across the three app verticals and explains the report’s dataset, coverage, regions, and date range.
key_points: The takeaways report global e-commerce app sessions increased 5%; LATAM finance installs and sessions rose 76% and 57%; and gaming retention remained flat, with day 1 at 27% and day 30 at 5%.
The methodology covers e-commerce/shopping, finance/fintech, and gaming across global, APAC, Europe, LATAM, MENA, and North America.
The dataset combines Adjust’s top 5,000 apps with the total set of apps tracked by Adjust, with data sources covering 45 countries and approximately 250 countries under the ISO 3166-1 standard.
The stated date range is January 2024–January 2026; the report says figures are aggregated and anonymized and may not represent the entire global app market.

sections.title: Gaming apps
sections.summary: Opens the report’s first vertical chapter, introducing the gaming-app benchmark before the dedicated “Finding and keeping users” analysis begins on page 17.

sections.title: Finding and keeping users
sections.summary: Analyzes gaming acquisition, sessions, retention, install costs, and partner networks across regions and subverticals for 2024–2025. The results show growth and retention patterns diverging by game type.
key_points: In “Gaming app install and session growth percentages YoY 2024 - 2025 (Global),” casual games grew 19% in installs and 37% in sessions; hyper casual grew 4% and 31%; strategy sessions rose 57% despite flat installs; casino and slots installs grew 22% and 46%, while sessions fell 5% in each.

For “Gaming app retention rates 2024 - 2025 (Global),” all games remained at 27% day 1, 13% day 7, 8% day 14, and 5% day 30 retention; hyper casual retention was 27%, 8%, 6%, and 2% at those same days in 2025. Global gaming CPI reached $0.56 in 2025, up 30%.
Regional install/session growth was mixed: MENA recorded +2%/+7%, Europe -7%/+3%, LATAM -9%/+0.4%, and North America -5%/-2% in 2025.
Gaming partners per app averaged 5.3 in 2025, down from 6 in 2024; hybrid casual, idle RPG, and simulation moved against that decline, increasing to 9.8, 6.7, and 6.8 partners, respectively.

sections.title: E-commerce/shopping apps
sections.summary: Opens the second vertical chapter, which proceeds to analyze e-commerce and shopping user acquisition, engagement, retention, and costs. The dedicated “Finding and keeping users” section begins on page 27.

sections.title: Finding and keeping users
sections.summary: Compares e-commerce growth and acquisition patterns across regions and subverticals, then examines retention, CPI, paid/organic mix, and partner counts. Overall sessions increased even as total installs declined.
key_points: In “E-commerce app install and session growth January 2024 - December 2025 (Global),” installs fell 10% year over year in 2025 while sessions rose 5%; LATAM led regional growth with installs up 17% and sessions up 30%.

For “E-commerce app retention rates 2024 - 2025 (Global),” day 1 retention declined from 13.2% to 12.6%, day 7 from 6.3% to 6%, and day 30 stayed at 3%. In “E-commerce app CPI 2024 - 2025 (Global),” overall CPI fell from $1 to $0.98, while deal discovery CPI rose from $1.44 to $2.26.

The global e-commerce paid/organic ratio increased from 0.48 in 2024 to 0.54 in 2025; MENA rose from 0.54 to 0.63, APAC from 0.43 to 0.49, and North America from 0.38 to 0.42, while LATAM and Europe declined.
E-commerce partners per app averaged 6.3 in 2025; deal discovery and marketplace/classifieds increased to 9 and 10, while shopping decreased to 6.

sections.title: Finance apps
sections.summary: Opens the third vertical chapter, followed by analysis of finance-app acquisition, engagement, costs, and channel mix. The dedicated “Finding and keeping users” section begins on page 34.

sections.title: Finding and keeping users
sections.summary: Examines finance-app installs and sessions, regional variation, retention, session length, CPI, paid/organic acquisition, and partner counts. Session activity rose substantially even as installs declined globally.
key_points: In “Finance app install and session growth January 2024 - December 2025 (Global),” installs fell 4% year over year in 2025 while sessions rose 21%; February installs were 14% below the yearly average and December installs were 8% above it.
For “Finance app install and session growth percentages YoY 2024 - 2025,” LATAM recorded +76% installs and +57% sessions; APAC recorded +5% and +50%; Europe +15% and +19%; and MENA +42% and +10%.

Global finance app session length rose 8% to 7.18 minutes in 2025; North America led at 8.43 minutes, while session length declined in APAC, Europe, and MENA. Day 0 sessions per user globally fell from 1.52 to 1.48.
Finance CPI fell globally from $1.51 in 2024 to $1.13 in 2025, while the global paid/organic ratio rose to 1.13; LATAM’s ratio increased to 3.26.

sections.title: Conclusion: An exciting future for the mobile app industry
sections.summary: Concludes that app growth depends on understanding whole, cross-device journeys and integrating attribution, AI insights, and optimization capabilities. The contents page lists the conclusion at page 41, while the displayed conclusion page is labeled 40.
key_points: The report characterizes finance apps as increasingly embedded in daily life, e-commerce as accelerating through AI personalization and agents, and gaming as balancing user acquisition with retention and sustained engagement.
It recommends integrated, adaptable, and accountable measurement and optimization foundations to reduce blind spots and support budget allocation based on aggregated data.

sections.title: About Adjust
sections.summary: Provides a short description of Adjust’s app measurement and analytics business and states the report’s data basis, variability caveat, and disclaimer. No printed page label is visible in the provided excerpt.
key_points: The report states that its data is aggregated and anonymized and comes from apps tracked by Adjust between January 2024 and January 2026.
It cautions that results may vary by vertical, region, and business model, and that forecasts based on third-party industry estimates are subject to change.
